newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends weak on Central Bank's cue.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends weak on Central Bank's cue.

text.p: * Central Bank estimated to have sold $125 million

The Philippine peso ended weak on Thursday at 26.285 pesos from 26.280 as banks went into a dollar-buying spree in late trade after the Central Bank lifted its offer rate for the dollar, traders said.
"Everyone was caught by surprise," a trader from a big bank said, when the Central Bank raised its dollar-selling rate to 26.285 from 26.28.
"No one knows why," another dealer said.
"It was a natural reaction for banks to buy dollars. It (the dollar) might still go up, so why don't we buy now," he added.
"We heard from the market foreign fund mangers were giving orders to close equity positions," said the first dealer. "So the Central Bank offered a higher rate."
One dealer estimated the Central Bank sold about $125 million at 26.285.

The day's average was at 26.283 to the dollar from 26.277 on Wednesday. The peso hit a day-low of 26.288 before recovering at close. Turnover was heavy at $259.80 million from $155.80 million. - LILIAN KARUNUNGAN (632) 841-8937
